Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

March 16, 2026

Lieutenant Chivas, Lieutenant Vasconcelos, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Director of Economic
& Community Development Jimenez, Director of I.T. Guadagnino, General Manager of Utilities Singh,
Director of Public Works Delgadillo, City Librarian Hassen, Senior Planner Alvarado, Economic Development
Manager Lopez, City Clerk Services Manager Juarez.

The Pledge of Allegiance was conducted.

The Invocation was led by Mayor Alvarez.

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Richman reported that no reportable action was taken in Closed Session.

CEREMONIAL

Presentation of checks from the 20th Annual Casino Night proceeds to local non-profit youth sports
organizations

Mayor Pro Tem Avila presented checks to several local non-profit youth organizations, including the Jr. Golf
Program, Canyon City Boxing, Azusa Raiders, Azusa Little League Baseball, and Azusa Little League Softball
in support of their programs and community involvement.

Recognition of the Azusa High School Girls Soccer Team

Councilmember Gonzales presented certificates to the Azusa High School Girls Varsity Soccer Team in
recognition of their achievement as runner-up in the CIF Championship. The team also received certificates
from the Office of Senator Susan Rubio.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Bruce Knowles, an elected Board Member of the San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District, expressed the
District’s support for the Azusa Aspen Well Project and the City’s water sustainability efforts; and briefly
referenced the Yuba Accord.

Venerable Nicolas Thanissaro extended an open invitation to the community to attend an “Open Day” at the
Buddhist Temple on East Monrovia Street on Saturday, April 4, in celebration of the Thai New Year.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Announcements

City Manager Gonzalez provided an update regarding the commencement of the General Plan Update, noting
that Staff are actively working to gather input from residents and community groups and will be attending
commission meetings to solicit volunteers for the advisory committee; and requested that the City Council
agendize an item in the near future to appoint a Council representative to the advisory committee.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Avila announced upcoming events at the Azusa City Library, including a Teen Craft event
featuring handcrafted clay mirrors on March 19; reported that free tire disposal will be available throughout the
month of April, hosted by Waste Management; congratulated all recipients from the Casino Night event and
thanked the sponsors, including Athens Services and Transtech.

Councilmember Mendez requested an update from the City Manager regarding the Rivers and Mountains
Conservancy and the agreement with the Watershed Conservation Authority (WCA); raised concerns regarding
the condition of asphalt along Azusa Avenue, noting that it appears incomplete and below standard; and

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
March 16, 2026
 inquired about the proposed hotel development at 725 North Azusa Avenue, commonly referred to as the Light
and Water building; and stated that he has received multiple questions from community members and requested
clarification regarding the current status and scope of the project.

City Manager Gonzalez responded to the inquiries stating that Staff will follow up with the Rivers and
Mountains Conservancy to arrange for a representative to provide an update; and explained that the project is
not an immediate development, but rather a future goal of the City Council to attract a quality hotel to the City;
stated that staff has been evaluating potential locations, including this site; further clarified that, as with any
proposed development, the item would be formally agendized for City Council consideration and would include
opportunities for public input.

Director of Public Works/City Engineer Delgadillo responded to the inquiry regarding the asphalt stating that
walkthroughs have been conducted with the contractor and that additional cleanup work will be completed.

Councilmember Bow announced upcoming events at the Azusa City Library, including Toddler Story Time on
March 19 and Family Bingo Night on March 24; shared that she participated in the 70th Anniversary of the
Azusa Little League Opening Day on March 14, as well as a listening circle held as part of the executive search
for the next Superintendent of the Azusa Unified School District; and encouraged residents to visit the
District’s website and participate in future listening circles and surveys.

Councilmember Gonzales announced a salsa dance class at the North Recreation Center on March 18, as well
as the annual Compost and Mulch Giveaway scheduled for April 4 at Memorial Park; introduced the “Pet of the
Month,” Mike, a 12-week-old male Akita mix available for adoption through Animal Care and Control; and
wished everyone a wonderful spring break and a Happy Easter.

Mayor Alvarez announced a St. Patrick’s Day Senior Social on March 19 at Memorial Park and extended Easter
holiday wishes to the community.

Councilmember Gonzales also congratulated City staff members Regina Sells-Arnold and Yesenia Paez, who
were recognized as Women of the Year by Assemblymember Blanca Rubio.

Councilmember Bow requested that the Azusa High School Decathlon Team be formally recognized at the
upcoming City Council meeting scheduled for April 6.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

CONSIDER AUTHORIZATION OF SERVICE AGREEMENT WITH INLAND VALLEY HUMANE
SOCIETY & S.P.C.A. FOR ANIMAL CONTROL SERVICES

Lieutenant Vasconcelos presented an analysis regarding the proposed transition of Animal Care and Control
services from Los Angeles County to Inland Valley Humane Society; explained that the City has contracted
with Los Angeles County since Fiscal Year 2012–2013, but following an evaluation conducted in Fiscal Year
2024–2025, Staff identified concerns related to responsiveness, operational reliability, and escalating costs,
which prompted consideration of terminating the agreement.

He noted that, with Council authorization, a termination notice was issued in December; outlined the
advantages of transitioning to Inland Valley Humane Society, addressed service concerns experienced under the
County contract, provided a cost comparison, and presented the recommended course of action.

Nikole Bresciani, President of Inland Valley Humane Society, provided a brief presentation detailing the
services offered by the organization; explained that the proposal includes a $100,000 capital infrastructure
investment, which may be paid either as a lump sum or over a two-year period; and stated that the service cost
for Fiscal Year 2026–2027 would be $574,517; and concluded by making herself available to answer questions
from the Council.

The Council engaged in discussion regarding the $1,000,000 capital improvement project and inquired about
what it covers. Staff responded that the capital infrastructure funding is allocated toward vehicles and kennel
improvements.

The Council also discussed the possibility of introducing a “Pet of the Month” program, noting that similar
efforts in the past yielded successful outcomes.
City Council Minutes  Page | 3
March 16, 2026
 Additionally, the Council requested a breakdown of service fees. Staff explained that all fees are included
within the overall cost, with no separate line-item charges.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales and seconded by Councilmember Bow and carried by unanimous vote of
the Council to: Approve the transition of animal control services from Los Angeles County Animal Care and
Control to the Inland Valley Humane Society & S.P.C.A. (IVHS), including authorization for a service
agreement with IVHS; and authorize the City Manager to execute a service contract with IVHS, in a form
acceptable to the City Attorney, for animal sheltering, field response, licensing, and enforcement services; and
approve necessary budget adjustments associated with the transition, including a one-time capital infrastructure
investment cost and revised service fees.

CONSIDERATION OF A FUNDING AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF AZUSA AND THE
AZUSA CHAMBER OF COMMERCE

Deputy City Manager Nico De Anda-Scaia presented a proposed funding agreement with the Azusa Chamber of
Commerce; explained that this item had previously been brought before the Council to reinitiate a partnership
with the City, at which time the Council directed Staff to meet with the Chamber to discuss terms for a joint
City–Chamber agreement; and noted that the prior agreement expired in 2024 and that the Chamber has since
undergone a significant transition.

He further explained that the proposed agreement outlines clear expectations for transparent business services
but includes several key items that remain undetermined and require Council discussion and direction prior to
adoption; and noted that Chamber representatives were present to answer questions.

The Council inquired about the Chamber’s annual budget for Fiscal Year 2025/26, employee wages, and
whether subcontractors are utilized. Chamber representative Jenni Bolivar responded that the annual budget is
approximately $65,000 and stated that, since assuming the role of CEO, her compensation has been about
$18,000; also confirmed that the Chamber does not currently employ subcontractors.

Discussion was held regarding upcoming revenue opportunities, as well as whether the Chamber has any
outstanding payables and what its proposed budget entails. The Council indicated that a comprehensive and
accurate financial report, including income, expenses, and a detailed budget, must be presented before moving
forward.

Moved by Mayor Alvarez, seconded by Councilmember Mendez, and carried unanimously by the Council to
direct staff to bring this item back for Council review once the requested information has been obtained.
